AI · Evaluation / Development note

A correct source does not guarantee a correct answer.

How to separate retrieval, citations and content when evaluating a document assistant. With questions, results and a reproducible run.

By Sergio Hernández7 November 2026
In this note
  1. Define the expected behaviour first
  2. Measure different layers
  3. Test the same path as the demo
  4. Publish failures too

An assistant can cite a real document and still fail to answer the question. To distinguish these behaviours, this website’s evaluation separates what retrieval finds, what the model writes and what the person ultimately sees.

Define the expected behaviour first

The public set contains twelve questions per language. Nine have a reference section; three have no answer in the library. Criteria are written before reviewing outputs and are not changed to make a run look better.

The question about an actual secret key shares vocabulary with a document recommending credential protection. That passage is topically relevant but contains no actual key. Retrieving it does not mean the question was answered correctly.

Measure different layers

Retrieval checks whether an expected section ranks first or in the top three. Provenance checks whether excerpts exist verbatim in documents. Content review checks whether an answer resolves the question without adding unsupported claims.

RAGAs distinguishes retrieval and generation dimensions; ALCE also examines citation quality. These studies inform the separation, but this lab uses its own checks: it does not run their tools or attribute their results to this prototype.

Test the same path as the demo

The evaluator imports the assistant’s index, context selection, generation contract and validator. Lightweight evaluation downloads no model. The optional run prepares Qwen3.5 in the browser and processes all twenty-four questions.

The exported record includes the question, retrieved sections, accepted answer or rejection reason, displayed sources and fingerprints of the evaluated components. If a relevant input changes, the build prevents a reference from silently becoming stale.

Publish failures too

Unsupported questions are part of the result. Word overlap can produce general advice where the system should acknowledge insufficient evidence. The lab retains that failure so the reader can inspect it.

The published review is AI-assisted and checked against the documents; it is not an independent human evaluation. A small set written for this library detects specific regressions, but demonstrates neither general accuracy nor universal safety or suitability for private data.

Putting it into practice

Evaluate retrieval, citations and claims separately. Keep negative cases and the execution record.

Cookies and privacy

What we store

The at_consent cookie remembers your choice for six months. Optional settings are stored locally for the same period. You can withdraw permission here: those settings will be deleted. Controls still work during your visit if you choose necessary only. If you enable the demo’s optional AI, the browser may store model files; delete them from the demo itself. Questions are not stored. The booking calendar connects to Cal.com only when you open it; booking details are handled under that provider’s privacy policy.

When you submit the form, your name, email, subject and message pass through Formspree to reach alejandro.dev.sergio@outlook.com. They are used to respond to your enquiry. The provider processes and stores details under its privacy policy. Do not include passwords or sensitive information.
